## PREFACE.

THE principles followed in the first volume in editing the hymns of the
Rig-veda, and in restoring the text of Sáyana's Commentary, have been strictly
adhered to in the second. My own conviction and the approval of those best
competent to judge have not allowed me to adopt a different course, although
others have thought Sáyana's Commentary undeserving a critical edition, and
the time that has been expended on it. Yet, perhaps, neither the age nor the
country of an author can justly be pleaded as an excuse for disregarding those
rules of critical scholarship which in classical philology have been ratified by
the experience of the last three centuries; and though I feel obliged to apologize
for the consequent delay in the publication of this second volume, I should be
more sorry if I had now to publish it without the conviction that all sources
available for the restoration of the text had been fully exhausted.

The MSS. of the Saṃhitá and Pada-text of the hymns have been the same for
the second as for the first volume, and therefore require no further notice.

<margin>3x</margin>The case differs with the MSS. of Sáyana's Commentary. For the first
Ashtaka I was able almost always to determine the original reading of each
of the three families of MSS. by a comparison of the different members belong-
ing to each; and it was found that in all important passages the readings of the
three families, A., B., and C., could be so easily balanced that it rarely remained
doubtful which of the three had to give way before the others. On this account
it seemed to me unnecessary to publish the *varietas lectionis* for the first Ashtaka ;
and, with the exception of a few inaccuracies which really seem to be unavoid-
able in the course of editing so voluminous a work, I have not met, in the many
excellent reviews of this edition of the Rig-veda, with any remarks which could
on this point have changed my opinion.

->VOL. II.<-
->b<-

<vocab>Rig-veda, Sáyana's Commentary, classical philology, Saṃhitá, Pada-text, Ashtaka, varietas lectionis</vocab>

<language>English</language>

<page-num>vi</page-num>
<header>PREFACE.</header>

In the second Ashtaka, however, this course could be no longer followed. When I began the printing of the second Ashtaka, to represent the A. class I had only one MS. instead of three, and this again was defective to such an extent that it could hardly be used for more than half of the second book. The MSS. of the B. class were the same as for the first Ashtaka; and I had even received a new copy from Bombay, which I call B 3. This, however, proved of little use, as it was but a new transcript of the same original from which Professor Burnouf’s MS. had been taken. It could not have been copied from B 1, because this MS. was already in my hands when the new copy was made in India. There can be no doubt, however, that it was copied from a copy of B 1. Most likely the Pandit who parted with his old MS. (B 1.) had a transcript made before he sold the original, and this transcript was copied in B 3. With regard to the C. MSS. it will be seen that three only out of the seven contain the second Ashtaka complete.

Under these circumstances it became impossible to determine with certainty the original reading of each of the three families; nay, for many passages the text of one or even two families was lost beyond recovery. Besides, almost all the MSS. of the second and the following Ashtakas seem to have been less frequently studied in India, and therefore less carefully corrected, than the first Ashtaka. The principal difficulty, however, arose from the defective state of A 2, because the text of the A. class is throughout the whole commentary by far the most authentic, and had been the principal authority for my edition. Before the first Ashtaka was finished I had therefore written to India to obtain a new MS. for the second. After waiting, however, for a considerable time, I received the news that the MS. which Dr. Roer had procured for me at Calcutta had been lost by shipwreck. Not wishing to retard the publication of the second volume still longer, I began to print with the MSS. then at hand. Most fortunately, in the course of carrying the second Ashtaka through the press, a new MS. was forwarded from India by Dr. Ballantyne, the distinguished Principal of the Sanskrit College at Benares. It was sent to Professor Wilson, and he most kindly presented it to me. It is a complete copy of Sāyaṇa’s Commentary, and, as far as I know, the most ancient MS. of this author in Europe. The first Ashtaka contains 648 leaves, but has no date. The second has 260, the third 398, the fourth 312 leaves. At the end of this Ashtaka the following date is given: ॥ संवत १६ ज्येष्ठबदि ५ शु वे १ संवत आषाढा २४ वर्षे ॥ This is Samvat

## Preface Text

1624 or A. D. 1681. The fifth Ashtaka has 237, the sixth 264 leaves, the last containing again a date; **संवत् १६२३ वर्षे ज्येष्ठमासे शुक्लपक्षे पूर्णिमास्यां पूण्यतथौ गुरुवनेः ।** This is therefore a year earlier, 1623 Samvat, or 1680 A. D. In the seventh Ashtaka, which contains 274, and in the eighth, which contains 322 leaves, the last leaves on which the date is usually marked, are lost. We may therefore ascribe this copy to the years 1680 and 1681. The oldest MS. which I had used before was that of the first Ashtaka at the National Library in Paris (A 1.), which bears the date Samvat 1625, or 1682 A. D. Colebrooke’s MS. (A 2.) was dated between 1747 and 1760 A. D.; and fragments of the Commentary to the first Ashtaka at the Royal Library in Berlin (A 3.) exhibit their date as Samvat 1664 and 1665, which is 1721-1722 A. D. As all the other MSS. of Sáyaṇa’s Commentary are still more modern, this last arrived MS., now in my possession, is therefore the oldest in Europe.

But though it is the oldest MS., it does not, as I expected, belong to the A. class. On comparing it with the other MSS. I found that it belongs to class C., and may in fact be considered as the prototype of all the C. MSS. This would by itself have made this copy extremely valuable. Its value, however, was further increased when I found that in the second Ashtaka considerable portions had been most carefully compared and corrected after a MS. belonging to the A. class. If it had not been for the modern date of Colebrooke’s copy, I should have said that the collation had been taken from this very MS. (A 2.) As it is, we must suppose that the Benares MS. was collated with an older A. MS., whence afterwards Colebrooke’s copy was taken. As these collations and corrections, which are very numerous, were made in the usual Indian manner, by covering the original text with yellow orpiment and writing the various reading over it, or on the margin, it was possible in many cases to use this MS. as an authority not only for the C. but also for the A. class; a discovery which makes this MS. invaluable, particularly for the second Ashtaka, where the text of the A. MSS. was frequently lost altogether. As to the C. MSS. they are all, though not immediately, derived from this copy, but *before* it had been corrected by a collation with an A. MS. This can be proved from accidental mistakes and indistinct corrections which occur in this MS., and have afterwards found their way into all the C. MSS. I suppose therefore that this (my own MS. from Benares) had been repeatedly transcribed there before it was collated with an A. MS.; that one of these transcripts was brought to Calcutta, and

<meta>This page is part of the preface to Max Müller's critical edition of the Rig-Veda. It provides a detailed discussion of the manuscript sources (codices) used, specifically distinguishing between the 'C' group (Calcutta manuscripts, including C1, C2, C3, and a manuscript from the Asiatic Society) and the 'A' and 'Benares' manuscripts. Müller explains how errors and conjectures were propagated by transcribers and describes his method for recording variant readings in the apparatus criticus. It mentions a specific textual variant in RV II. 6. 4. to illustrate the relationship between the MSS.</meta>
<vocab>C. MSS., A. MSS., Benares MS., Asiatic Society, varietas lectionis, apparatus criticus, Sáyana</vocab>

## Preface

that from it most, if not all, of the C. MSS. were taken at Calcutta. Certain it is that C 1, C 2, and C 3. came from Calcutta, and large portions, which were copied for me from a MS. belonging to the Asiatic Society in Calcutta, contain literally the same text as the other C. MSS. There are readings, however, which are peculiar to the C. copies, and which do not occur in my Benares MS. Some are found in one or two of the C. copies only. These are either accidental mistakes, or occasional conjectures, which, after finding their way into one copy, were afterwards repeated by successive transcribers. They are useful as indicating the exact relationship of some of the C. MSS., but they can never claim any diplomatic authority. There is another class of various readings which run through all the C. MSS., but which have no guarantee in the old Benares C. They deserve a more careful consideration, for they are evidently old errors, or possibly old corrections. In passages where the C.'s agree among themselves, but differ from the Benares C., this generally agrees with A. These C. readings therefore, as they do not proceed from the Benares C., are in reality only later alterations of the original A. text. Though I have hardly ever adopted the readings of the C.'s, where they differ from the A.'s and the Benares C., I have inserted them in the *varietas lectionis*, because occasionally they seem to contain useful conjectures. Thus Rv. II. 6, 4. (page 445. line 10.) Ca. has **प्रेरका वा ;** the same mistake occurs in A., while all the C.'s have the correct reading **प्रेरको वा.** It also happens, as has been shown in the Preface to the first volume, that passages originally wanting in the C. family have been supplied from other sources. In this manner C. and A. readings have been mixed up together in one and the same copy, particularly in Dr. Mill's, so as to cause considerable confusion in some parts of Sáyana's work. In later portions of the Commentary some of the C.'s cease to be C.'s, and become A.'s, owing to the writer having changed the original from which he copied.

By this new MS., which in its original text I count with the C., in its corrections with the A. MSS., while if it has to be quoted by itself, it will be marked Ca., the *apparatus criticus* became much simplified. The various readings of the C. MSS. have no longer any authority by themselves, but only so far as they agree with the original C. before it was collated. The text of the A. MSS. is supplied by Ca., where the A.'s are wanting, and confirmed where they and the corrections in Ca. agree.

It might be asked, why, if the A. MSS. agree with the corrected text of Ca.,

<meta>This page contains part of the scholarly preface to Volume II of Max Müller's edition. It details the process of textual collation and the genealogy of the manuscripts (sigla A., C., Ca.). The author argues for the independence of manuscript group A from the corrections in Ca by analyzing specific scribal errors and marginalia in the Rig-Veda and Sayana's commentary.</meta>

## Preface Text

the whole family of the A.’s should not rather be considered as branching off from Ca., *after* the general text of the C. family was corrected as we find it in Ca.? and why the alterations in Ca. should not be taken for independent corrections made by the writer of Ca., instead of being gleaned from a collation with an A. MS.?  On all important points the A. MSS. agree with the corrected Ca.; and on minor points it is impossible to deny that slight differences could as well be ascribed to the several copyists of the A. MSS. There are passages, however, which make it impossible to entertain this supposition: Rv. II. 9, 3. for instance, <term>उदीरिष्व</term> in Ca. has been corrected into <term>उदारिष्व</term>. Here the C. MSS. have <term>उदीरिष्व</term>, because they were copied from Ca. before it was corrected. But A. also has <term>उदीरिष्व</term>. This by itself might be a mistake of the copyist of A.; but this peculiar mistake is not likely to have happened if A. had been copied from Ca., where this very mistake had already been very distinctly emendated. I have selected this passage for another purpose also. It shows that occasionally corrections are made in Ca. which cannot be traced back to A. They generally refer to such palpable errors, as for instance <term>उदीरिष्व</term> instead of <term>उदारिष्व</term>; and in these cases it is clear that the intelligent writer of Ca. was guided by his own judgment without looking to the authority of any MS. In order to prove that A. was copied from Ca., it would be necessary to point out passages where corrections in Ca. had been misread by the writer of A. This happens not unfrequently with the C. MSS. Alterations made by the original writer of Ca. were mistaken by the later copyists, and these mistakes are occasionally of such a character that they could only have happened with the very leaf of Ca. before the eyes of the copyist. Now I have not been able to find any evidence of this kind against the A. MSS. Quite at the beginning of the second Ashṭaka, for instance (page 1. line 9), Ca. reads <term>ऋत्विग्भ्यान्त्यस्माह्वयति परिभाषया</term>। The writer seeing that he had left out <term>रि</term> between <term>षे</term> <term>ति</term>, made a mark at the top of <term>षे</term>, and wrote <term>रि</term> on the margin. The copyist of the first C. MS. mistook this mark for a vowel, and without looking to the margin wrote <term>°हृषेति</term>। A. however has <term>°हृयेरिति</term>। The same happened Rv. II. 6, 4, where Ca. had <term>सूरिर्विद्वान्</term>। This the original writer himself corrected into <term>सूरिर्विद्वान्</term>, only that the space did not allow him to do more than to make a mark at the top of <term>वि</term>, and to draw a slight line between <term>र्</term> and <term>व</term>। The copyist of C. mistook this for <term>सूरिर्वैद्वान्</term>, which henceforth became the reading of the C. MSS. Indeed it looks very much like <term>सूरिर्वैद्वान्</term> in Ca. A. however reads <term>सूरिर्विद्वान्</term>। Rv. I. 181, 8. (p. 366. l. 24.) Ca. had originally <term>जलहूः</term>

<meta>This page (Roman numeral x) is part of the editorial Preface to Max Müller's edition of the Rig Veda. It contains a critical discussion of manuscript traditions, comparing readings between manuscripts A, B, Ca, and the C-class. Specifically, it addresses textual variants in Sāyaṇa's commentary for Rig Veda Mandala III (Hymns 1 and 7) and the second/third Aṣṭakas, detailing scribal corrections and the genealogy of the source manuscripts.</meta>

## Critical Notes

**प्रदानविशेषो वा.** Accordingly all the C.’s read **जलरः.** A. however has **जलदः,** and from it the correction is made in Ca., where, subsequent to the taking of the first C. copy, the **र** was covered with yellow, and changed into **द. जलरः** is evidently an old mistake, because it occurs in B. also. Rv. III. 1, 8. (p. 626. l. 14.) the C. MSS. have **जनुषा जन्म मनुष्याणां**, thus leaving out two lines. The omission was originally made by the writer of Ca., but afterwards supplied on the margin from A. That it was not supplied from B., but from A., can be proved by the words **स्वत एव बंधुरिति यावत्**, which are not in B., but in A. only. At the beginning of the third Aṣṭaka (Rv. III. 7, 1.) the invocation in Ca. is simply **श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥ ओं वागीशा** etc. It is the same in the C.’s. A 2. has **श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥ श्रीसरस्वत्यै नमः ॥ श्रीगुरुभ्यो नमः ॥ ॥ वागीशा** etc. The B.’s have **श्रीगणेशाय नमः श्रीगुरुभ्यो नमः ॥ वागीशा ;** only B. (Taylor) has a slight correction **श्रीगणेशाय** etc. Coincidences of this kind though they may seem irrelevant are really the most convincing. Again, Rv. III. 7, 1. (p. 661. l. 7.) A 2. has **त प्र य क्षारेः**, while Ca. and the C.’s have the right reading **तत्र प्र य क्षारेः.** In the same verse (p. 662. l. 3.) A 2. has **शितिपृष्ठशब्दस्य;** Ca. and the C.’s coincide in giving **शितिपृष्ठस्य . पृष्ठशब्दस्य .** Rv. III. 7, 2. (p. 663. l. 11.) Ca. has **द्वितीयायां** instead of the more primitive reading **द्वितीयाैकवचनांतस्य**, which is in A 2. and B. The C.’s have again **द्वितीयायां** like Ca. As no case of this kind can be made out against A., it is necessary to regard the corrections in Ca. as collations from a MS. which was connected with the A. class. How A. and Ca. came originally to differ, is hard to say. But as it is impossible to account for the text of the one simply as a corruption of the other, A. and Ca. must be considered as two branches diverging from the original stock of Sāyaṇa’s work which is lost to us. A. and Ca. are coordinate, not subordinate, though A. stands higher than Ca. B. also stands independent from A. and Ca. The C. MSS. on the contrary are subordinate to Ca., or, as in later portions of the Commentary, to A., and must therefore be discarded where the evidence for a reading has to be weighed by the authority of MSS. Even in cases where the C. MSS., particularly C 2. and C 5., contain large portions of the Commentary which are taken from an A. MS., they are of very little use for restoring the original text of A., except occasionally in the second Aṣṭaka where A 2. is defective. Here C 5. (Wilson 74.) has sometimes supplied the deficiency, but the modern date and general incorrectness of this MS. hardly allow us even then to ascribe much weight to its readings.

If we compare the three MSS., A., Ca., and the C.’s at the beginning of the

In **कृतकृत्याः** (p. 1. l. 2) Ca. had left out the **Visarga**, and it is wanting in the C.’s. It was afterwards added in Ca., above the line, **कृतकृत्याः**, and it stands above the line in A. also. P. 1. l. 6. Ca. had **ज्ञेया** instead of **ज्ञेया**. **ज्ञेया** became the reading of the C.’s, while in Ca. it was altered into **ज्ञेया**, which is the reading of A. P. 1. l. 7. Ca. had **शतनामाद्धे**, which was corrected by the writer himself (not *secunda manu* or with yellow orpiment) into **शतर्चनामान्ने**. This correction was therefore adopted by the C.’s, and it is also the reading of A. P. 1. l. 8. Ca. had **°नुवाकैः**; one of the vowels was afterwards covered with yellow. The C. P. 1. l. 11. Ca. had **प्र वो ग्नेयदेवं**. Here the copyist of the first C. MS. must have corrected the mistake, which was indeed very palpable, for the C.’s read **वैश्वदेवं**, which is also in Ca., but as a correction. P. 1. l. 11. Ca. had **अस्य विशेपो लैंगिकः**. Thus the C.’s have **अस्य विशेपो लैंगिकः**. Ca. was afterwards corrected into **विशेषविनियोगो लैंगिकः**, but in such a manner that none but a learned copyist could have made out the correction. A. however has the right reading. P. 1. l. 17. Ca. had **पाललशीलं**, which became the reading of the C.’s. In Ca. it was altered into **पालनशीलं**, by putting १ over **ल**, and २ over **न**, and covering part of **न** with yellow. A. has distinctly **पालनशीलं**. This was, not at all distinctly, corrected into **दुरितं वा तस्य द्रावयिते**, which is the reading of A. But the old mistake remained in the C.’s. On looking more closely, however, we find that the *i*, before it was covered with yellow, was already struck out with ink *prima manu*, which accounts for the adoption of the corrected reading in the C.’s. There is one more MSS. of Sāyaṇa which has come to hand since the publication of the first volume, and which, though rarely quoted in the *varietas lectionis*, deserves to be mentioned here. It was sent to me as a present by Mr. T. Edward Hall of Benares, to whose zealous exertions Sanskrit literature is already greatly indebted. Unfortunately it is but a fragment, beginning with the twenty-seventh Varga of the third Adhyāya of the third Ashṭaka, and ending at the end of the third Ashṭaka. But it is of great importance in so far as it served to confirm those principles of diplomatic criticism on which all the other MSS. of Sāyaṇa had been previously classified, and according to which their respective weight and authority had been determined. Its title is **संवत् १६२४ वर्षे ॥ ॥ आषाढवदि ११ बुधे लिखितं ॥ श्रीरस्तु ॥ ॥ कल्याणमस्तु ॥ ॥ शिवमस्तु सर्वजगत परहितनिरता भवंति । भूतगणा दोषा प्रयांतु नाशो स्तु सर्वत सुखी भवतु लोकाः ॥ ॥ कल्याणं भूयात् ॥** This shows that its age is exactly the same as that of Ca.; Samvat 1624, or A.D. 1681. Its readings would therefore have had considerable weight whether they coincided with any of the three classes or not. But on a close examination it was found that not a single reading, not even a mistake, occurred in this MS. which was not known already from the A. MSS. Nay, I feel almost convinced that Colebrooke's A. MS. was copied directly from the fragment which is now in my possession. Rv. IV. 2, 13. (vol. III. p. 18.) the whole explanation of the thirteenth verse had been left out in Aa., but was afterwards added so as to cover the whole margin, not without giving rise to many ambiguities by the indistinctness of the letters. All these ambiguous letters are reproduced with the greatest exactness in Colebrooke's MS., where the explanation stands no longer in the margin, but forms part of the Commentary. A still clearer case occurs Rv. IV. 4, 4. (vol. III. p. 35.) Here also the Commentary on verse 4. had been left out in Aa., and been supplied as far as the space allowed on the margin. ## Editorial Notes

If we compare the readings of the two MSS., and remember that both came from Benares, there can hardly be a doubt that the latter (A 2.) was copied directly from Aa. It is clear that the writer of Colebrooke's MS. was misled by the marginal notes of Aa., that he left out all that was written on the right margin, and went on from the end of the second line to the third line on the left margin. After having proceeded to the end of the verse he became aware of his mistake, and then added the whole omitted passage on the margin. This is nearly convincing. But there are other points to show that A 2. is a direct descendant of Aa. The **हष्ण** in **तीक्ष्ण** is very indistinct in Aa.; a blank is left in A 2. The **घ** in **ज्वालासंघं** looks, according to Aa.'s style of writing, very much like **थ**; A 1. has **थ**. In VOL. II. d

--- Page 18 ---
<lang>English</lang>
<page-type>preface</page-type>
<page-num>xiv</page-num>
<header>xiv PREFACE.</header>
<meta>This page contains the conclusion of a preface section discussing manuscript transmission (specifically comparing manuscripts Aa., A 2., and Ca.), followed by a "Varietas Lectionis" (critical apparatus) section for Rig Veda Mandala I, Sukta 122.</meta>

**उधतात ।** the **Virāma** under **त** is covered in **Aa.** by the **हि** of the next line; the writer of **A 2.** did not perceive this, and thus altered **ता** into **त्त**. In **Aa.** the marked **द्धि** in the fourth line is meant as a correction of the marked **द्धि** in the third. The writer of **A 2.** began his marginal notes with the fourth line, mistook the third as an addition to come in after the marked **द्धि**, and thus wrote **द्धिमिति हीं** instead of **मिद्धिर्ही**. **शतवं** in **Aa.** would look exactly like **शास्त्रानं** to one not familiar with the peculiar style of writing used in these marginal notes; in **A 2.** we find **शास्त्रानं**. Other coincidences between **Aa.** and **A 2.** require no explanation. The only real difference between the two is **निरंतरां** in **A 2.** instead of **नितरां** in **Aa.**; a mistake evidently produced by the distraction of the writer, and the omission of the passage between **कुरुते** and **कुरुते**. This will be sufficient to show that **Aa.** is really the prototype of the **A. MSS.**, and that therefore, if the whole of this **MS.** could have been recovered, it would have rendered to the **A. class** the same service which was rendered to the **C. class** by **Ca.**

## Critical Notes

P. 13. l. 17. (123, 4.) **प्रतिहतमुद्योगं प्रकाशनरूपं ॥ प्रतिगृह्णद्योगं प्रकाशनरूपं** A. Ca. **प्रतिहतमुद्योगे प्रकाशनरूपं** C. **प्रतिहतमृद्योगप्रकाशरूप** B.

P. 15. l. 17. (123, 7.) **परिक्षपयतोर्वा ॥ परिक्षपयितोर्वा** B. **परिक्षपयतोवा** A. Ca. **परिक्षितोपि** C.

P. 16. l. 4. (123, 8.) **न दृश्यंते** A. Ca. B. **नश्यंते** C.

P. 16. l. 5. (123, 8.) All the MSS. read **स चैकविंशतिघटिकाभि: षड्विंशतिपराभिश्च संमित: ।** except B., which has **पराभि संमित: ।** There is no doubt a mistake in this part of the Commentary. A day consists of 60 Ghatikás, a Ghatiká of 60 Kalas, a Kala of 60 Nimeshas, a Nimesha of 30 Tatparas: cf. Bháskara’s Guṇitádhyáya, I. 21, translated by Dr. Roer; Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal, No. CXLV. p. 55. Now if, according to Sáyaṇa, the sun’s daily course is 5059 Yojanas, which is the equatorial circumference of the earth, (cf. Bentley, Historical View of the Hindu Astronomy, p. 185,) the thirty Yojanas which are ascribed to the duration of twilight cannot correspond to 21 Ghatikás and 26 Paras, even if it were possible to take Para in the sense of Tatparas. The numbers 21, 26, however, are such that they seem to be based on calculation, though on a very inaccurate one. For

-> 30 Yojanas = 30 / 5059 × 60 × 60 Kalas <-
-> = 21 + 1761 / 5059 <-
-> And 1761 / 5059 Kalas = 60 × 1761 / 5059 Nimeshas <-
-> = 20 + 4480 / 5059 <-
-> or 30 Yojanas = 21 Kalas + 20 4480 / 5059 Nimeshas. <-

We get still nearer to Sáyaṇa’s numbers if we put the approximate value 1 / 168 for the fraction 30 / 5059. This gives 30 Yojanas = 21 Kalas + 25 5/7 Nimeshas.

P. 16. l. 10. (123, 8.) **उदिता** B. C. (?) **उदितो** A. Ca.

P. 16. l. 23. (123, 8.) **यमकोट्यां ॥ यवकोट्यां** A. Ca. B. **ययवकोट्यां** C. Cf. Reinaud, Mémoire sur l’Inde, p. 341; and Rája Rádhakanta’s Sabda-Kalpa-Druma s. v.

P. 17. l. 19. (123, 10.) **जनांतिके विवसना** A. Ca. B. **वसना** C.

P. 21. l. 18. (124, 3.) **सम्यगानयिती** (**सम्यग्मानयिती** is a misprint) **सम्यगनयिती** A. Ca. **सम्यगमनयिती** B. **सम्यगनपिती** C. If the causative of **श्रण** could be formed with a short **श्र**, the reading of A. would be correct.

P. 25. l. 2. (124, 7.) **तां तु सभ्या विचार्य यदीयं रिक्थं लभते चेदक्षै: संताड्य तदीयं धनं वितरंति** A. Ca. There is evidently a mistake in the grammatical construction of this sentence. It lies either in **चेद्** or in **संताड्य**. No help is to be derived from the various readings of the MSS. B. has **छेद्दक्षै: ;** C 2. reads **यदीयं रित्थं लते चेदक्षै: संतोष्च ;** C 5. **तांतं सभ्या विद्या विचार्य** and **संताल्म**. The Commentary on the Nirukta is of no use for the grammatical restitution of the text, but as it explains the custom alluded to by

<meta>This page contains critical philological notes and manuscript variants for Max Müller's edition of the Rig Veda, specifically focusing on Mandala 1, Suktas 129, 130, and 131. It compares readings between manuscripts A, B, C, and Ca, discussing grammatical issues in Sāyaṇa's commentary (bhāṣya).</meta>

## Critical Notes

यथा **तिष्ठति सेवन्त्ययति**, and C. **तिष्ठति अवन्त्ययति** । The mistake probably lies in **तिष्ठति**, instead of which a locative might be expected of a word meaning ‘precipice,’ or something similar, into which water falls and disappears. Two verbs like **तिष्ठति** and **नश्यति** put together without a copula is against the usual style of Sāyaṇa. It would be irregular also to join **स्रवन्** or **विस्रवन्** to words like **तिष्ठ** (loss, disappearance, end) or **विष्ठ** (fæces), reading **तिष्ठनिस्रवन्** instead of **तिष्ठति स्रवन्**. Still less could **तिष्ठति** be taken for a locative, or in the sense of standing water (**सरसि**).

**P. 65. l. 9. (129, 10.)** All the MSS. read **महते प्रीतये** instead of **महत्यै प्रीतये**. It is possible that Sāyaṇa himself wrote **महते**, intending to add, as he frequently does, **अवसे** or **रक्षणाय**. In this case he would have made the adjective agree, not with **प्रीतये**, but with **रक्षणाय**. As it is, the authority of the MSS. must give way before the claims of grammar.

**P. 66. l. 12. (129, 11.)** Instead of **तमिन्द्रं देवा न व्यसृजंतेत्यादि**, B. reads **तन्मिंद्रो देवता ह्वं सृज्यंतेत्यादि**; C. and A. **तमिंद्रो देवान् विसृज्यंतेत्यादि**. We might read **तमिंद्रं देवा व्यसृजंतेत्यादि**, taking **विसृज्** in the sense of ‘creating,’ as it is frequently used in vaidik as well as epic works. This would correspond better with the text of the hymn, where it is said that Indra was created by his father to destroy the evil spirits. The words of the Commentator are probably a quotation from a Brāhmaṇa, and may thus still receive a safer correction.

**P. 70. l. 6. (130, 4.)** Instead of **स्वोपयोगाय** (A. C.), B. reads **यागाय**, which with reference to the Yūpa gives a good sense; but it is evidently a later correction of the transcribers. Ca. reads **प्रयोगाय**, and has **स्वो** in the margin.

**P. 70. l. 27. (130, 5.)** Instead of **यस्मै कस्मैचित्समर्थाय तदर्थं**, A. and Ca. sec. man. read **यस्य कस्यचित्समर्थाय तदर्थं**, C. **यस्य कस्य न समर्थाय तदर्थं**. In B. the whole sentence from **यथा वा** to **यद्वा** is left out. I have corrected it, because it seemed too ungrammatical for the time of Sāyaṇa to have the pronoun in the genitive joined to a substantive in the dative. Similar barbarisms occur, however, in later works and less erudite authors.

**P. 74. l. 14. (130, 9.) ततः करोति पूर्वं** A. B. C.

**P. 74. l. 24. (130, 9.) यथा त्वोतेन** A. C. **यथा चोरोणेण** B. (**चोरेण**?).

**P. 75. l. 10. (130, 10.) आष्टमिकमाद्युदात्तत्वं** A. B. C. It refers therefore to Pāṇ. VIII. 1, 19, and in particular to **अपादादौ** of VIII. 1, 18. The **आद्युदात्तत्वं** can be called **आष्टमिकं** only in a negative sense, or by way of **प्रत्युदाहरणं**.

**P. 78. l. 4. (131, 3.) यस्य गृहानित्यादिनैमित्तिकवा** ॥ **यस्य गृहानित्यानै** A. **यस्य गृहानित्यानै** C. Ca. **यस्य गृहनित्यनैमित्तिकाकाम्यवा** B.

**P. 78. l. 13. (131, 3.) किं हि वचनेन कुर्युन्नास्ति** B. **किं हि वचनं न कुर्या नास्ति** C. **किं हि वचनं न कुर्युन्नास्ति** A. Ca.

**P. 79. l. 16. (131, 4.) इमान्यपकार्याणि** ॥ **इमानि अपकार्याणि** A. Ca. **इमानि अपकार्याणि** C. **इमानि अप: कार्याणि** B.

## Critical Notes

P. 80. l. 6. (131, 5.) **युद्धाय हि धीराः संभजंते ।** A. C. **यद्वा ये धीराः संभजंते** B.

P. 80. l. 7. (131, 5.) **संग्रामवासिनस्वव्यन्यमन्यामन्यांन्यान्त्श्च ॥ ˚नः त्वय्यन्यामन्यां** C. **˚नः त्वय्यन्यामन्यां** A. Ca. **˚नः ॥ त्वयि अन्यामन्यां** B.

P. 80. l. 11. (131, 5.) **इत्यादिदेशे ॥ इत्यादिदेशे** C. **इत्यादिदेशे** A. Ca. B.

P. 80. l. 24. (131, 6.) **अपि नाम जानीहि** B. **अपि नाम तावकमसत्** A. Ca. sec. m. **नावकमसत्** C. Ca. pr. m.

P. 81. l. 2. (131, 6.) **गुणाप्रतिषेधाभः ॥ गुणाभावः** A. B. C.

P. 82. l. 10. (132, 1.) Instead of **हे मघवन् । मघः सौख्यं । तद्विंद्र**, which is the reading of A. and C., B. has the more usual explanation, **हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र ।**

P. 82. l. 11. (132, 1.) The Commentator explains **इन्द्रोताः** as a compound without adverting at all to the irregularity of such a composition. The Pada-text does not separate **इन्द्र** from **ओताः**, and I have therefore left it as one word. If **ओताः** is to be taken in the sense of 'protected by thee,' it must of course be separated from **इन्द्र**, whilst if **इन्द्रोताः** is one word, the first part is probably **इन्द्रत्व** in the sense of 'the power of Indra,' and the whole means 'protected by the power of Indra.' The question is only how far we are allowed to alter the accent of the word. **त्वाऽउताः** is a common expression; **इन्द्रत्वाऽउताः** occurs but once more in a hymn of Sobhari, VIII. 19, 16, where Sāyaṇa explains it again by **ईश्वरेण त्वया उता रक्षिताः संतः ।**

P. 82. l. 14. (132, 1.) The words **पूर्व्ये धनेऽस्मिन्यज्ञे** belong only to B., and may be a later addition. It often happens where Sāyaṇa leaves words in the text without explanation, that the writers of B. supply them by conjecture.

P. 83. l. 11. (132, 2.) All the MSS. read **करोतेः शतरि.**

P. 84. l. 20. (132, 3.) **प्रकाशं** A. B. C. **प्रकारं (?)**.

P. 85. l. 14. (132, 4.) **तमेव यष्टारं** B. The Commentator seems to distinguish between **क्वचिदव्रतं**, which he explains by **अयज्जानं**, and **हृणायंतं चिदव्रतं**, i. e. **अस्मासु रोषं कुर्वंतमेव यष्टारं.** A. and C. however read **कुर्वंतं तमेवायष्टारं ।**

P. 87. l. 19. (132, 6.) This quotation from Śaunaka refers to his Rig-vidhāna, of which two MSS. exist in the E. I. H. Collection, No. 1732. Both leave out the second verse from **ता जपन्** to **समश्रुते ।** which is found, however, in all the MSS. of Sāyaṇa. In the first verse A. Ca. read **उभे पुनामीति सूक्ते सप्तर्चस्तु प्रकीर्त्तिताः ।** C. **सप्तर्चे सुप्रकीर्त्तितोः ।** I have adopted the text of B. **उभे पुनामीति पुरा रिपुध्न्यस्तु प्रकीर्त्तिताः ।** as it coincides with both the MSS. of the Rig-vidhāna, only that 1732 a. reads **परा** instead of **पुरा.** For the same reason I have adopted **नियच्छति** at the end of the third verse; it rests on the authority not only of B., but also of the Rig-vidhāna MSS. 1732 a. and b. A. and C. read **निकृंतति** instead.

P. 88. l. 2. (133, 1.) I am not quite certain whether **महीः** is explained by **उर्वीः ।** The passage is wanting in B.; A. Ca. sec. m. read **महीः तुवीः**, Ca. pr. m. and C. **महीः सवीः ।**

P. 90. l. 19. (133, 6.) **द्युलोक आश्रयभूतः ॥** द्युलोकः आश्रयभूतः B. द्युलोको नामाश्रयभूतः A. द्युलोका-

P. 97. l. 27. (135, 1.) After **नियुता**, B. adds **नियुद्भिरागच्छेति शेषः । यद्वा.**

P. 102. l. 16. (135, 7.) **प्रियतय्यात्मिका** A. B. C. instead of the more usual **प्रिय सत्यात्मिका**.

P. 106. l. 11. (136, 2.) **संगतम्भूत् ।** A. and C. read **संगतोऽभूत्**, while B. leaves it out
altogether. Perhaps it is a repetition from the preceding line; but if it is at all
to be repeated here, it must be **संगत** instead of **संगतो**. The same fault occurs
again in all the MSS., line 14, **संगतोऽभूत्** instead of **संगतम्भूत्**.

P. 106. l. 16. (136, 2.) All the MSS. have **यद्यपि**, and again **तथा यद्यपि**. The sense,
however, would become much clearer if the first **यद्यपि** was omitted.

P. 106. l. 20. (136, 2.) **दधाते । धारयतः । दधाये ।** A. Ca. **दधाप्ये धारययः ।** C. **दधाये । धारयथः** B.
And again line 22, **दधाये** A. C., **दधाये** B. P. 107. l. 8. also, all the MSS. have **सचेथे**
instead of **सचेते**, but explain it by **भवतः ।**

P. 107. l. 6. (163, 3.) Here again Sāyaṇa's Commentary follows a different
text from that which we find in the MSS. of the Rig-veda. All the MSS. read
**धारयत्क्षितिं** as one word, while Sāyaṇa explains it as two, **धारयत् क्षितिं**, which is
evidently wrong.

P. 108. l. 25. (136, 5.) Here also instead of **पातः । परितो रक्षतां ॥** A. C. have **पाथः । परितो
रक्षतं ।** B. **पातः । परितो रक्षतं ।** Cf. p. 106. l. 20.

P. 112. l. 9. (137, 2.) **सोमासः सोमा—तमिति शेषः ।** A. Ca., except that they read **दध्याश्रयण°**

B. has **सोमासः सोमाः ग्रावभिः इभिषुताः संपन्नाः अत आयातमिति शेषः । दध्याशिरः ॥ दध्याश्रयणवंतः इमे—तमिति

P. 113. l. 7. (137, 4.) **केवल औणादिकोऽरप्रत्ययः ॥ केवल सौणादिको अरिप्रत्ययः ।** A. Ca. B. **केवल

<meta>This page is part of the preface to Max Müller's edition of the Rig-Veda. It contains critical apparatus and discussion of variant readings found in different manuscripts (sigla A, B, C, Ca) for Sayana's commentary on Rig Veda Mandala 1, Suktas 138, 139, and 124. It cites Pānini, the Nirukta, and the Prātiśākhyas to justify editorial decisions regarding verse fillers (pādapūraṇa) and difficult readings.</meta>

## Critical Notes

Pāṇ. VI. 1, 134. **सोऽचि लोपे चेत्पादपूरणम्** ; VI. 1, 57. **गो: पादांते** ; and VIII. 1, 18. **अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादौ**. In the Nirukta I. 9., however, we read **अथ ये प्रवृत्तेऽर्थेऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रंथेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छंति पदपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेषु**, and I find no various reading in the MSS. of the Nirukta or of its Commentary. In the Prātiśākhyas again we have **पादपूरण**, as Pr. A. XII. 103. **क्रियावाचकमख्यातमुपसर्गो विशेषकृत् । सत्वाभिधायकं नाम निपातः पादपूरणः ॥**

P. 116. l. 9. (138, 4.) **पूष्णामेदं** । A. Ca. **पूषरणामेदं** C. **पूषणा मिदं** B.

P. 116. l. 10. (138, 4.) **ओ इति ॥ अञ्जा: ओ इति ॥** A. Ca. B. **अञ्जा: अं इति ॥** C. These readings have probably arisen from the word **अञ्जा:**, which had occurred several times before, and was still in the mind of the transcribers. It is evidently an old mistake. Either it owes its origin to a mere *lusus memoriæ*, or, what is more likely, it is a corruption of **आह उ** instead of **ओ**.

P. 116. l. 14. (138, 4.) **यद्वा आहूणे ॥ यद्वा आहूणे** A. **यद्वा आह्वन्** C. **यद्वा आहूयमान** B.

P. 118. l. 9. (139, 2.) **त्वद्दृष्टैः** and **त्वदासक्तेन** A. B. C. instead of **युष्मद्दृ°** or **तद्दृ°**

P. 118. l. 10. (139, 2.) **आत्मीयै रन्यैश्चक्षुरादींद्रियैः ॥ आत्मीयैरन्यैश्चक्षु°** A. C. **आत्मीयैरिंद्रियैः** B. But line 11, B. reads **अस्मदीयैश्चक्षुरादींद्रियैर्नासन्नं**, while A. has **अस्मदीयैरिंद्रियैः मनासन्नं**, C. **अस्मदीयै-रिंद्रियैः स नासन्नं**.

P. 119. l. 23. (139, 4.) **वां युवयोर्वंधुरे** C. **वां युवयोर्वधुस्त्वय** B. **युवां युवयोर्वंधुरे** A. Ca. The reading may have been **वां युवां युवयोः** ; but it is not unlikely that Sāyaṇa himself wrote **वां युवयोः**, though **युवां** would have made the sentence much clearer. That Sāyaṇa himself had not written **युवां**, I conclude from this, that **वंधुरे**, which is here left out in B., is some lines further down wrongly inserted after another **वां युवयोः**. It is curious, however, that **वंधुरे** should occur after this second **वां युवयोः**, not only in B., but in A. also, though in A. it had been inserted in its right place. **वां युवां युवयोः** would be the best reading, and might be defended by A. and Ca.

P. 119. l. 25. (139, 4.) **स्थाम । अवस्थापयाम ॥ स्थानं स्थापयाम ।** B. **स्थानं तस्थापयामास ।** C. Ca. pr. m. **स्थाम स्थापयामास ।** A. Ca. sec. m.

P. 121. l. 25. (139, 7.) **आवाहनं ।** A. B. C.

P. 122. l. 12. (139, 7.) **लब्ध्वेव वा लोपस्त इति तलोपः ॥ लब्ध्वेव** Ca. A. (but Ca⁵. has **ल - व वा**) **लभ्येव वा लोपस्त इति लोपः ।** C. **लोपस्त इत तलोपः ।** B.

P. 124. l. 5. (139, 9.) The last lines of the Commentary contain several difficult passages, probably owing to defects in the original MS. C. leaves out the words from **अस्माकं** to **जन्मा**, and instead of **संबद्धा यागा वा**, A. Ca. read **संबद्धा या गावः**, B. **संवंधा यागा वा**. The most difficult sentence, however, is the following : **असौ विशिष्टजन्मा वो यदा योग्ये इति तैर्वक्तव्यत्वेन तदधीनत्वं ।** A. Ca. C. leaves out the first words and begins **अवो यदा योग्ये इति निर्वक्तव्यत्वेन तदधीनत्वं ।** B. again has **असौ विशिष्टा जन्मा चौ यदा योग्ये इति ॥ तैर्वक्तव्यत्वेन तदधीनत्वं .** None of these readings can be the right one, and I was obliged to write by conjecture **असौ विशिष्टजन्मा वो यज्ञयोग्य इति तैर्वक्तव्यत्वेन तदधीनत्वं .** **दा** or **ड्र** is a common mistake for **ज्ञ** in Sanskrit MSS. The sense would be, ‘These old sages know my noble descent, and as they live amongst the great Rishis they can tell them...

**P. 157. l. 13. (144, 5.)** अधिशब्दोऽनर्थको धात्वर्थमात्रानुवादी ॥ अधिशब्दानर्थके त्वात्वर्थमात्रानुवादी A. Ca. (त्वात्वं Ca⁵.) अधिशब्दो र्थको धात्वर्थमात्रानुवादी C. अधिशब्दो नर्थकत्वाद्धात्वर्थमात्रानुवादी B.

**P. 173. l. 5. (149, 2.)** Instead of प्रापयति, Prof. Wilson proposes प्राख्यायति, which would certainly be more appropriate; but all the MSS. have प्रापयति.

**P. 173. l. 7. (149, 2.)** यद्यग्निन्नं पचेत् पूरयेदेव नोत्पद्यते A. Ca. B. यद्यग्निना पचेत् ॥ पूरयेदे C. Ca⁵. (पूरयेदैव B₃.) I conjecture यद्यग्निन्नं पचेत् पूर्णदेहो नोत्पद्येत. Prof. Wilson, whom I consulted on this passage, gives the following explanation: "I do not think any conjecture is necessary, but that उत्पद्यते may be used impersonally, or with *id* or *tad* for its nominative. 'When Agni does not mature or verily fill (or satisfy), it is not produced; that is, nothing is produced, production does not take place.' The construction is elliptical, but not unintelligible. With reference, however, to the phrase पश्वादिदेहाकारेण, देहो might be inserted, but it is not indispensable."

**P. 176. l. 24. (150, 3.)** In the Chándogya-upanishad (VII. 10), from which these words are taken, the text is मासेभ्यः पितृलोकं पितृलोकादाकाशमाकाशाचंद्रमसमेष सोमो राजा.

**P. 177. l. 16. (151, 1.)** तच्चैकया द्वित्वादपि स्यात् A. तच्चैकया द्वित्वादभिस्यात् Ca. C. तच्चैकया द्वित्वाद्भिस्यात् B. The sense is that गव्यः expresses merely the possession of cows, even where a man possesses (or wishes to possess) only a few of them; गोषु, the

plural, is therefore added to show that many cows are intended. One expects something like **तच्चैकगोस्वामित्वादपि स्यात्**, or **तच्चैकद्वित्वादपि स्यात्**, but neither is quite satisfactory. Prof. Wilson proposes **तच्चैकया द्वित्वादि** or **एकया द्वित्वाद्यपि स्यात्**, explaining it by "in this place by one (or the singular), two, three, or more may be;" that is, he who wishes for a cow, means he who wishes for many cows; as Gopati, ‘lord of a cow,’ means ‘lord of many cows,’ etc.

**P. 192. l. 22. (154, 4.)** The quotation from the Chandogyāraṇyaka is evidently made from memory, and therefore not very accurate. As it is difficult to correct Sāyaṇa’s text, I add the passage from the original (VIII. 2 and 3): **स त्वेव सोम्येदमग्र आसीदेकमेवाद्वितीयं तदैक्षत बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति । “तत्तेजोऽसृजत” । तत्तेज ऐक्षत बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति तदपोऽसृजत । ता आप ऐक्षंत बह्व्यः स्याम प्रजायेमहीति ता अन्नमसृजंत ॥ ॥ सेयं देवतैक्षत हंताहमितिस्रो देवता अनेन जीवेनात्मनानुप्रविश्य नामरूपे व्याकरवाणीति तासां त्रिवृतं त्रिवृतमेकैकां करवाणीति ॥** Instead of **हंताहमिं**, A. and C. read **हंतमिं**, B. **हंतेमं**.

**P. 193. l. 6. One of them has already been received into the text by B 2. and B 3. Both of them add **मायावीजादितिरभिगदिते सत्यपि** after **परमेश्वरस्य**. B 1. has as a marginal note to **मध्व उत्सः**, **अमृतस्योत्पत्तिः वर्तते;** and it gives **सुकर्मणां** in addition to **सुकृतीनां**. But these notes have not found their way into B 3.

This page is part of the Preface to Max Müller's edition of the Rig-Veda-Sanhita. It contains detailed editorial notes and a critical apparatus comparing various manuscripts (A, B, C, D, S 3). The notes primarily concern textual variants in the commentary of Sāyaṇa for Mandala 1, Suktas 157 to 161. ## Critical Notes

P. 204. l. 22. (157, 6.) Instead of **रथ्येभिः**, S 3. has **रथ्येभि।**

P. 205. l. 3. (157, 6.) Before **आ वां**, A. has the words **सर्वत रथा युवां**, C. **सर्वत रथयो वां** or **सर्वत रथयो वां.** They are wanting in B., and refer to another hymn addressed to the Aśvins.

From the beginning of the third Adhyáya to the end of Varga 13. I possess fragments of a MS. which was procured for me at Calcutta. It is a modern copy, but it contains very useful readings, and the original from which it was copied seems to have been an excellent MS. I ascertained, however, that the Pandit who copied it for me had occasionally inserted corrections of his own. On this account the readings of this MS. ought to be tested by their own intrinsic value only; and in the few cases where the MS. had to be quoted I have called it D., because it cannot claim a place in any one of the three historical families of Sáyana's manuscripts.

P. 208. l. 11. (158, 4.) **एवमवध्यं तं वैतनो** A. C. **एवमवध्यं त वितनो** B.

P. 208. l. 18. (158, 4.) **दशतयो दशवारः ॥ दशतारः** A. B. C. **दशतयोऽपरिमितावयवः** (cf. **Pán. V. 2, 42**) **दशतारः** D.

P. 209. l. 24. (158, 6.) **वलीपलितगात्रो.** All the MSS. read **वलीपलितगात्रो**, where **पलित** is too unusual an expression to be retained. However, **वलीपलितगात्रो** also is not satisfactory, and the reading of D., **बलिवलितगात्रो**, offers at least a probable conjecture.

P. 212. l. 4. (159, 3.) **जज्ञुः । ज्ञातवंतः** A. C. sec. m. **ज्ञातवंतः** B. Ca. pr. m. C.

P. 213. l. 1. (159, 5.) From here to 161, 3. A 1. is wanting (p. 213—218).

P. 214. l. 12. (160, 1.) **उदकोत्पादनायाप्रयत्नत्वावित्यर्थः ॥ ॰त्नमयतीत्यर्थः** B. **॰त्नवमती इत्यर्थः** C. **॰त्नवतीयर्थः** D. D. explains **कवि** by **शब्दमुदकं**, while B. and C. leave it unexplained. **शब्दयदुदकं** would be better.

P. 214. l. 13. (160, 1.) **वृष्ट्युदकधारयत्सूर्योपिते ॥ धारीवित्सू** B. **धारवित्सू** Ca. **धारिवित्सू** C. **धारित्सू** D.

P. 215. l. 19. (160, 3.) **विश्वाहा** is not explained in B. and C. D. supplies it as usual.

P. 216. l. 11. (160, 4.) **लिटि रेफसामान्यात्** Ca. sec. m. **रेसामान्यात्** B. Ca. pr. m. C. This refers to **Pán. VII. 4, 71: चृकारैकारैशस्य रेफस्य हल्व्वे न ग्रहणादिहापि नृत्.** D. has **रभ्युतिसामान्यात्.**

P. 219. l. 19. (161, 4.) D. adds **ऋभुपैरिदं वाक्यं** at the beginning of the fourth verse. None of the other MSS. have it.

P. 220. l. 12. (161, 5.) **उपहवकाले** B. **उपहूव** C. A. or **उपहूव.**

P. 220. l. 26. (161, 6.) **परस्ताच्च ॥ पुरस्ताच्च** A. B. C.

P. 221. l. 1. (161, 6.) **विश्वरूपमित्यस्याश्च पंक्तिरिति** B. D. **विश्वरूपाविति च तस्याश्चपंतिरिति केचन** A. **विश्वरूपािमिति च तस्याश्च पंक्तिरिति** C.

P. 221. l. 5. (161, 6.) **इत्येवमृहिराह ॥ ॰मिमाह** A. B. C.

P. 222. l. 8. (161, 8.) **अथवा ऋभूनप्रति तस्यैवेदं वाक्यं** A. B. C. D. writes **मंतस्वेव** by conjecture. **तस्य** however refers to **ऋभोः.**

P. 223. l. 23. (161, 10.) **पिंशति । अपरे ॥ पिंशति पित्रोः अपरेः** A. B. C. D. has **पिंशति पित्रोरपरे.** Perhaps **पित्रोः** belongs to **तयोने किंचिद्**, and may have been an old marginal gloss.

P. 226. l. 14. (161, 14.) **अन्तरिक्षात्** after **द्युलोकात्** would better be omitted; but it stands in A. B. C. D.

P. 226. l. 24. (162, 1.) The words from **अङ्गानि** to **शिट्ठा** are wanting in A. and C. B. has **अधिवपेत्** instead of **आवपेत्**. D. adds **अस्मात्पुरस्तात्** after the first **शिट्ठा**, with reference to the following **इत्यस्मात्पुरस्ताद्वा**.

P. 228. l. 2. (162, 2.) After **शतृ** D. adds **यद्वा छांदसः शपः सुः। एरनेकाच इति यण्॥**

P. 228. l. 17. (162, 3.) I have added the words **अहोरात्रे — उक्तत्वात्** from D., as the meaning of Sāyaṇa would scarcely be intelligible without them.

P. 229. l. 11. (162, 8.) All the MSS. have **श्ववपोरित्यल्लोपः (त्वलोप: B.)**, though in A. and C. it looks more like **श्ववपो**. I cannot find the passage in Pāṇini to which this quotation refers. The rules for the nominative singular of the word in question are Pāṇ. III. 2, 71, 1 and 2. **श्वेतवहादीनां डस्.** D. therefore adds after **चल्लोपः** the words **श्ववयाः श्वेतवाः पुरोडाशेति निपातितः.** Cf. Pāṇ. III. 2, 71, 3, and VIII. 2, 67.

P. 229. l. 13. (162, 5.) **प्रशस्ता** A. B. C. **प्रशस्त** D.

P. 230. l. 1. (162, 6.) D. reads **उत अपि च ये यूपार्हस्य खिन्नस्य काष्ठस्य चाढारः॥**

P. 230. l. 7. (162, 6.) **बलेन** A. B. C. **फलेन** D.

P. 230. l. 16. (162, 7.) **प्राप्तपार्श्वभागः** B. **प्राप्तपार्श्वीद्भाग** A. Ca. **प्राप्तावाश्र्वोद्भाग** C. D. has **पश्चाद्भागः**, which would correspond better with **पृष्ठः**.

P. 233. l. 1. (162, 12.) **यथास्माभिरश्व उपालब्ध एवं स्पृहयंति॥ यथास्माभिरश्व उपालब्धेर एवं स्पृहयंति B. यथाश्वाभिरश्व उपालब्धे एवं स्पृहयंति A. Ca. यथाश्वाभि अश्व उपालब्धे एवं स्पृहयंति C. यथास्माभिरश्व उपालब्धे एवं स्पृहयंति D. Or अस्माभ्यमश्वे? or अस्माभिरुपलब्धेऽश्वे?**

P. 233. l. 7. (162, 13.) **मांस्यचन्याः**, S. I. 2, 3. P. I. 2. See, however, Prātiśākhya I. 4, 101.

P. 234. l. 1. (162, 14.) **यद्वा बंधनं वट् तद्भूतं प्रदेशं** A. C. B. has **षट्.** Some words are wanting to complete this sentence. **तद्वान्प्रदेशः**, however, is not likely to have been the original reading.

P. 234. l. 20. (162, 15.) **यद्वा इष्टं प्रयाजैराप्रीतं वीतं पर्यग्निकृतं** A. B. C. **यद्वा इष्टं प्रयाजे वीतं प्रीतिरापयर्यग्निकृतं** D. It would be better to read **यद्वा इष्टं प्रयाजैः वीतमाप्रीभिः पर्यग्निकृतं**, but the MSS. are against it.

P. 234. l. 21. (162, 15.) **अभिगुर्तं ये यजामह इत्यागूर्त्योक्तं॥ अभिगुर्तं ये यजामह इत्याग्नेय्र्युक्तं** A. **ये यजामह इत्यागूरुक्तं** B. **ये यजामह इत्यागूर्युक्तं** D. **अभिगुर्तं ये यजामह इत्यागूर्युक्तं** Ca.; lacuna in C. The reading of D. seems the best, and might have been adopted. The **आगूः** precedes the **याज्या, याज्यादावागूर्भवतीत्युक्तत्वात्.**

P. 235. l. 7. (162, 16.) Instead of **चात्वाले** (A. B. C. D.), Prof. Wilson proposes to read **चषाले.** See verse 6.

P. 235. l. 16. (162, 17.) **अर्थतोऽगमनं कुर्वन्** A. C. **दर्पतो गमनं कुर्वन्** B. D.

P. 235. l. 17. (162, 17.) **पार्ष्ण्या** requires a gloss, **पादाधोभागेन.**

P. 235. l. 18. (162, 17.) **यत् यस्मात् तस्मात्ते तव**; left out in A. B. C., and supplied from D.

P. 236. l. 7. (162, 18.) **इदमवद्यमिति** A. Ca. **इदमवद्यमिति** B. **इदमद्यमिति** C.? **इदमवद्भरमिति** D.

P. 236. l. 14. (162, 19.) **एकः । एक एव । स कः ॥** एक एव तत्स कः A. C. **एकः एक एव तत्सकः** B. **एक एक एव स एकः** D.

P. 237. l. 4. (162, 20.) **केवलमांसग्रहणेषुः** D. **केवलमांसग्रहणे** A. B. C.

P. 238. l. 10. (162, 22.) **समूहार्थे यत्** A. B. C. D. According to Pánini it should be **यः**।

P. 240. l. 9. (163, 3.) **दुर्द्दिनरूपेण** A. C. **दुदिनेरूपेण** B. D. has **दुर्द्निरूपेण** (**दुर्द्निरूप्येण** ?), which might seem preferable if it rested on the authority of MSS. The same applies to **योगादिसामध्नं** (A. B. C.), instead of which D. has **यागादिसामधनं**.

P. 242. l. 6. (163, 6.) **आदित्यमंडलादप्युपरिभूतैः** A. and C. have **पश्यान्त्युपरिभूतैः**, leaving out the whole sentence between. B. has preserved it, but reads **प्रादित्यमंडलादित्युपरिभूतैः**. D. reads **आदित्यमंडलेष्वपरिभूतैः**.

P. 244. l. 15. (163, 10.) **शीघ्रधावनाय** D. **श्रीः प्रधावनाय** A. B. C.

P. 244. l. 24. (163, 10.) **यदापन्दिव्यं°** A. B. C. D. or **यु**. The Nirukta and its Commentary (Durga) have **यदापन्दिव्यं**, which corresponds better with the Aorist **आक्षिषुः**.

P. 246. l. 17. (164, 1.) **द्विपंचाशदृचं ॥ द्विपंचाशत्यृचं** A. B. C.; and again (p. 247. l. 18.) **चत्वा- रिंशदृचं ॥ चत्वारिंशत्यृचं** A. B. C.

P. 247. l. 21. (164, 1.) A. is wanting from 164, 1—164, 16 (p. 247—258).

P. 248. l. 21. (164, 1.) **संंरा्भानि**. The Brihad Áraṇyaka, from which this passage seems to have been taken, reads **संहृब्भानि**. Cf. Brih. Ár. p. 616.

P. 249. l. 2. (164, 1.) **ख्वरसत्त्वाभावात्** B. Ca. B. in marg. **प्रकरणवि रोधी** instead of **ख्व**. **प्रक- रणविरसत्वात्** ?

P. 249. l. 15. (164, 2.) **किं वस्तुतः सप्त** Ca. sec. m. **किंच वस्तुतः सप्त** C. **किंच स्तुतः सप्त** B. Ca. pr. m.

P. 249. l. 27. (164, 2.) **तिस्रो नाभिस्थानीयाः संध्याः संबद्धा वा तय ऋतवो यस्य ॥ तिस्रो नाभिस्थानीयाः संबंधानाद्ये ये ऋतवो यस्य** B 1. (**तिस्रो संबंधानाद्यय** B 3.) **तिस्रो नाभिस्थानीयाः संबंधा वा तय ऋतवो यस्य** Ca. C.

P. 254. l. 10. (164, 8.) **हलमुखेन ॥ हलमुखे** C. **वलमुखे** Ca. **जलमुखे** B. **हल्युक्तैः** ?.

P. 255. l. 24. (164, 11.) **द्वादशसंख्याकमेषादिराश्यात्मकैश्चै र्ैः रथांगावयवैर्युक्तं** B. C. The words **द्वादशसंख्याकमेषादिराश्यात्मकैश्चै** seem to be a later addition, inserted in the wrong place. The original reading was probably **द्वादशसंख्याकैश्चै रथांगावयवैर्युक्तं**, and after this the words **द्वादशसंख्याकमेषादिराश्यात्मकैश्चै** were to be added.

<meta>This page contains critical notes and variant readings for the Rig Veda Sanhita, specifically for verses in Mandala 1, Sukta 164 (verses 12, 13, 16, 19, 20, 21, 23). The notes compare different manuscripts (MSS A, B, C, Ca.) and discuss interpretations of Sayana's commentary and related Vedic texts like the Tandya-brahmana and Asvalayana Sutras.</meta>

## Critical Notes

**P. 256. l. 16. (164, 12.)** **परायत्तं** Ca. **पयीयतं** B. C.

**P. 257. l. 5. (164, 13.) आ तस्थु:** is not explained in B. or C. except by **वर्तं इत्यर्थ:**. As **इत्यर्थ:** is generally preceded by a more literal explanation, it is likely that the omission is owing to the copyists, and not, as in other cases, to Sāyaṇa himself.

**P. 259. l. 5. (164, 16.) लक्षणोऽस्ति स ईं ॥ लक्षणोऽस्ति स: स ईं** B. **लक्षणास्तिस्त स ईं** C. **लक्षण-स्त्रिस: स ईं** A. **लक्षणास्तिस: स ईं** Ca. sec. m. (**यो** pr. m.)

**P. 259. l. 9. (164, 16.) लौकिकोक्तिरिरियं** B. **लौकिकोऽग्निरियं** A. Ca. sec. m. (**रि** pr. m.) **लोकि कोनिरियं** C.

**P. 259. l. 23. (164, 16.) इत्युपक्रम्य—मंत्रकृदिति** B. A. and C. enlarge on this passage, as happens frequently in quotations from Brāhmaṇas. After **उपक्रम्य**, A. has first **ते**, which belonged probably to **ते देवानपृच्छंत**, and then, after repeating the words from **शिशुवांगिरसो** to **आंमंत्रयत**, A. goes on **तं पितरोऽब्रुवन्नधर्मं करोषि** etc. C. agrees with A. except that **तं पितरोऽब्रुवन्** follows at once after **उपक्रम्य**. In Ca. the words from **शिशुवौ** to **स उजदुजयति** stand in the margin. A. Ca. and B. have **मंत्रप्रदहृ:**, C. **मंत्रदहृ:**. The whole passage from the **Tāṇḍya-brāhmaṇa** (13, 3.) is this: 
> **शिशुर्वा आंगिरसो मंत्रकृतां मंत्रकृदासीत् । स पितृन् पुत्रका इत्यामंत्रयत । तं पितरोऽब्रुवन्नधर्मं करोषि यो न: पितृन्सतः पुत्रका इत्यामंत्रयस इति । सोऽब्रवीदहं वाव पितास्मि यो मंत्रकृदस्मीति । ते देवानपृच्छंत (देवेष्वपृ°)। ते देवा अब्रुवन् एष वाव पिता यो मंत्रकृदिति तद्वै स उदजयत् ॥**
See also **Manu II. 151.**

**P. 261. l. 15. (164, 19.) चक्रुयु: कृतवंतौ तानि;** these words are omitted in all the MSS.

**P. 262. l. 8. (164, 20.) जीवादन्यो जीवाश्रयत्वात्** B. **जीवादन्यो ना जीवाश्रयत्वात्** A. Ca. **जीवादन्यो ता जीवाश्रयत्वात्** C. If **जीवादन्यो** be the right reading, we should perhaps also read **जीवात्मा परमात्मनोऽन्य:**. A. Ca. and B. however have **नान्य:**, and C. also has **न्नन्य:**.

**P. 262. l. 10. (164, 20.) वास्तवाभेदं चापे°** C. **वास्तवभेदं वापे°** B. **वास्तवभेदं चापे°** Ca. A.

**P. 262. l. 23. (164, 20.) अनीशया** Ca. correct. C. **अज्ञनीया** A. (**ज्ञनीया** Ca.) **ऽनीया** B.: cf. **Muṇḍaka Upanishad III. 2.**

**P. 263. l. 6. (164, 20.) न च तद्वावा नाझो तन्म°** A. Ca. C. **न च तदा वात्रान्यो** B. **न च तद्वावान्यो** is not likely to have been the original reading, but neither **तद्वावादन्य:** nor **तद्वावनाझो:** would be much better.

**P. 264. l. 5. (164, 21.) मदन्य:** A. C. deest in B.

**P. 264. l. 8. (164, 21.) परमात्मभूवं ॥ परमात्मा भूतं** A. Ca. B. **परमात्मभूतं** C.

**P. 266. l. 9. (164, 23.) शोंसावोमिति** etc. In explanation of these sacrificial formulæ B 1. gives the following marginal notes: 
> **होता प्रातःसवने शोंसावोमिति मंत्रेणाध्वर्युमाह्वयते । तस्यायमर्थः । हे अध्वर्यों शोंसावः शंसनं कुर्वतः । ओमित्यनुज्ञार्थं । त्वयानुज्ञा दियेत्युक्तं भवति । सोऽयं त्र्यक्षरो मंत्रः । ततोऽध्वर्युः शंसामोदैवोमिति पंचाक्षरेण प्रतिगृण्हाति । उत्तरं ब्रूयात् । तस्यायमर्थः । होतस्त्वं शंसनं कुरु । त्वामोमोदैव । हर्ष एवास्माकं । अतोऽनुज्ञा दत्ता । तदेतन्मंत्रद्वयं मिलित्वाष्टाक्षरं संपद्यते । एवमुत्तरत्र ज्ञेयं । होता शस्त्रं पठित्वा उक्थं वाचीति चतुरक्षरं मंत्रं ब्रूयात् । मदीयायां वाचि संपत्रं । तस्यार्थः । ततोऽध्वर्युंरुक्थशा इति चतुरक्षरं मंत्रं ब्रूयात् । ओमित्यंगीकारे । उक्थशास्त्रं शस्त्रशंसी भवतीत्यर्थः । तदेतन्मंत्रद्वयं मिलित्वाष्टाक्षरं संपद्यते ।**
In the Commentary on **Āśvalāyana** the following explanation is given: 
> **शोंसावेति शंसावेत्यर्थः । स एव प्रणवांतः शोंसावोमिति पठ्यते ॥ शोंसामो दैवेति प्रतिगरो भवति । शंसामो दैवोमिति वा ॥**

<meta>This page contains a set of critical notes from the preface of Max Müller's edition of the Rig-Veda. These notes provide textual corrections and manuscript variants for the commentary on Rig Veda Mandala 1, Sukta 164 (the famous "Asya Vamasya" hymn). It references manuscripts designated as A, B, C, and Ca, and provides linguistic analysis for specific Sanskrit phrases in Sayana's commentary.</meta>
<vocab>एतदेवेकादशाक्षरं, अध्वर्युं, एकस्यामृच्य्यारूढं, यद्यन्नं, प्रतिपादनमेदाद्, बालकस्याञ्जनपानादि, एजृ कंपने, महदहंकारौ, अविकृतिरूपाया, मूलप्रकृतेः, अर्द्धगर्भाः, आरंभणशब्दादिभ्य, वेदान्तसूत्र, परोक्षज्ञानं, सात्विकजातेः, वाक्यपरिमिता</vocab>

## Critical Notes

**P. 266. l. 23. (164, 23.) एतदेवेकादशाक्षरं भवति ॥ एतदेवावाशाक्षरं भवति** A. C. **एतदेवाद्वा** (**द्वा** over **द**) B. The next sentence from **अध्वर्युं** to **भवति** is left out in A. and C. It is not clear how the words of the Hotri can be said to contain eleven syllables except by allowing for Vaidik productions; the words are the same in Āśvalāyana V. 50.

From 164, 24. to the end of the hymn A. is wanting (p. 267—291).

**P. 267. l. 13. (164, 24.) एकस्यामृच्य्यारूढं ॥ एकस्यामृच्य्यूगूढं** Ca. C. **एकस्यामृच्यागूढं** B.

**P. 269. l. 6. (164, 26.) यद्यन्नं इत्यतपत् ॥ यध्वां इत्यपतत्** B. **यध्वं इत्युपतत्** Ca. C.

**P. 269. l. 7. (164, 26.) तत्तद्देशोऽभिज्ञः** C. **तत्ताद्दृशोऽभिज्ञः** B. Ca.

**P. 270. l. 24. (164, 28.) प्रतिपादनमेदाद्** Ca. **प्रतिभादनभेदाद्** C. **प्रतिभेदनभेदाद्** B.

**P. 271. l. 10. (164, 29.) बालकस्यादनस्तनपानादि° ॥ बालकस्याञ्जन°** Ca. (**ञ्ज°** C.) **बालकस्याञ्जनपानादि°** B.

**P. 271. l. 27. (164, 29.) एकान्वश्रयणेन वा** Ca. C. **एकान्वाश्रयणेन वा** B.

**P. 272. l. 21. (164, 30.)** The line which the MSS. give here might perhaps be placed before **जीवस्य वैलक्षण्यमाह** (p. 273. l. 3).

**P. 273. l. 1. (164, 30.)** B. explains **एजत्** by a marginal note **एजृ कंपने**.

**P. 273. l. 2. (164, 30.) शयैतेषु ॥ शयैतेव** Ca. pr. m. C. **शयैते** B., and in marg. **रपः**. It should be **सा शेते च**; and this seems to be intended by some indistinct corrections in Ca.

**P. 277. l. 4. (164, 36.) महदहंकारौ ॥ मदाकारौ** C. **मदाहंकारौ** Ca. **महकारौ** B. **प्रकृति** being written over it.

**P. 277. l. 5. (164, 36.) अविकृतिरूपाया विकाराश्रयाया मूलप्रकृतेः ॥ अविकृतिरूपाः विकाराश्रयायाः मूलप्रकृतौ** Ca. C. **अविकृतिरूपा विकाराश्रयाः मूलप्रकृतौ** B. The words **अविकृतिरूपा विकाराश्रयाः** cannot be applied in their technical sense to the **महदाद्याः प्रकृतिविकृतयः सप्तः**, but only to the **मूलप्रकृतिरविकृतिः**. The genitive is better than the locative on account of the following **च**. In a wider sense **अविकृतिरूपाः** might be taken as an explanation of **अर्द्धगर्भाः**.

**P. 277. l. 17. (164, 37.)** After **अनुगतोऽस्मि**, B. has **अस्ति भाति प्रियमिति**; Ca. reads **अनुगतोस्ति भातित्रियमिति**, C. **भानित्रियमिति**, which is unintelligible. **भावत्रयमिति** or **भावित्वमिति** is not satisfactory.

**P. 277. l. 22. (164, 37.) तदनन्यत्वमारंभणशब्दादिभ्य इति** Ca. B. C. has **आरंभशब्दा°**, but **आरंभण** is the reading of the Vedānta-sūtras, II. 1, 15.

**P. 277. l. 24. (164, 37.) यदिदं यत्परोक्षं ॥ यदिवा यदापरोक्षज्ञानं** C. B. (**ज्ञा** corrected in Ca.)

**P. 277. l. 24. (164, 37.)** After **परोक्षज्ञानं**, B. leaves out the words from **ज्ञानं** to **ज्ञानं**. C. has **तदित् । तद्वदेवमस्मि इदं सर्वमहस्मीति ज्ञानं** (**तदित** Ca.)

**P. 278. l. 24. (164, 38.) स्थानः । यत्र ॥ स्थानतवय** Ca. C. **स्थानतवय** B., and in marg. **अवस्थातव्य**.

**P. 279. l. 7. (164, 38.) सात्विकजातेः । तं ॥ स चत्विजाते तं** B. **स चत्विजातेः तं** Ca. C.

**P. 284. l. 16. (164, 44.) छेदनेन नापितकार्यं ॥ छेदनेनापि तत्कार्यं** C. B. **छेदनं नापितकार्यं** Ca., which would have been adopted, if the MSS. had been then at hand.

**P. 285. l. 3. (164, 45.) परिमिता ॥ वाक्यपरिमिता** B. **वाक्यपरिमित्ता** Ca. C.

## Critical Notes

**P. 285. l. 17. (164, 45.)** याज्ञिकैः समाम्नातोऽनुष्ठेयार्थप्रकाशको वेदभागो मंत्राः । मंत्रविधान° ॥ याज्ञिकैः समाख्यातो नुष्ठेयार्थे प्रकाशदिमंतविधानं **Ca.** याज्ञिकैः समाख्यातो नुष्ठेयार्थे प्रकाशदिमंतविधानं **C.** याज्ञिकैः समाख्यातोऽनुष्ठेयार्थे प्रकाशदिमंतविधानं **B 1.** (ष्ठेयार्थ **B 3.**) All the MSS. have mixed the explanation of the Mantra with that of the Kalpa; the former is अनुष्ठेयार्थप्रकाशक, the latter मंत्रविधानप्रतिपादक. The quotation **इति मंत्राः कल्पोऽत ऊर्ध्वं** is of frequent occurrence in the Brāhmaṇas. **B 1.** takes it as a quotation from a Sūtra, and has in the margin **सूत्र प्रथमाध्याय खं° ४.** Some of the Sūtras differ very little from the Brāhmaṇas, and some Brāhmaṇas contain considerable portions written in the style of Sūtras. Thus Kumārila says, **आरुणपराशरशाखाब्राह्मणस्य कल्पेरुपनं.** Sāyaṇa, in his Introduction to the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa, writes **कल्पस्त्वारुणकेतुकचयनप्रकरणे समाम्नायते । इति मंत्राः कल्पोऽत ऊर्ध्वं यदि बलिं हरेदिति.** See Prolegomena, p. 144.

**P. 286. l. 1. (164, 45.)** वाच्यस्य **B.** खाख्यस्य **C.** खाख्यस्य **Ca.**

**P. 288. l. 6. (164, 48.)** नाभ्यरिहाणि. This is the reading of the MSS., which may be meant for नाभ्यभिधानि or नभ्याभिधानि; but the cerebral *n* seems to point to something else: cf. *Pán.* IV. 2, 80.

**P. 291. l. 19. (165, 1.)** The quotation from the Rig-vidhána required some alterations. **A.** (which begins again with this hymn) has **कया शुभेति पैशुन्यं श्रुत्वा चायं नृपद्विजां ;** **C.** has **कया शुभेति पशुत्यं श्रुत्वा चायं नृपद्विजां (Ca.** पै°); while the text of the Rig-vidhána is in one MS. **कया शुभेति पाशुन्यं कृत्वा चार्यै नृपद्विजैः,** in the other **कया शुभेति पैशुन्यं कृत्वाचार्यनृपद्विजैः.**

**P. 295. l. 8. (165, 7.)** यद्यस्यैव तन्नस्यैव भवतु । तन्मस्यै ॥ यद्यस्यैव तुन्मस्यै **A. C.** अद्यस्यैव तुन्मस्यै **B.**

**P. 297. l. 16. (165, 12.)** मस्कृत्तः ॥ त्वत्कृतैः **A. B. C.** It might be मत्कृतैः or युष्मत्कृतैः.

**P. 302. l. 12. (166, 6.)** विक्षेपणशीलं दंती ॥ विक्षेपणशील दती **C.** विक्षेपणशीतदती **A. Ca.** विक्षेपणशील दंती **B.**

**P. 309. l. 5.** From 167, 4—171, 6. **A.** is wanting (p. 309—328).

**P. 315. l. 13. (168, 4.)** After **अपापाः; Ca. C.** give quite a different explanation to the end of the verse: **अपापाः समुद्रतेनेन पांसु विचुः व्यावर्येति । चालयतीति ॥** It seems to refer to **अरेणवः**, but the text is corrupt.

**P. 323. l. 19. (170, 1.)** नैव नास्ति **B. Ca. C.**

**P. 324. l. 3. (170, 2.)** अस्मन्तनपराधिनः **B.** अस्मन्मपराधिनः **Ca. C.**

**P. 327. l. 10. (171, 3.)** Between **इंद्रश्च** and **सुखयंतु B.** and **Ca. C.** have **यूयं.**

**P. 327. l. 20. (171, 4.)** अस्मन्तनपराधिनः **B.** and **Ca. C.** have **अस्मान्नपराधिनः.**

**P. 330. l. 16. (173, 2.)** खेदुहव्यैः स्वायत्तेडाविष्कैः । यद्वा स्वयं प्रामेधकं हव्यं येषां **B.** खेदुहव्यैः स्वायत्तेडाविष्कैः । यद्वा स्वयं प्रामेधुं उदकं हव्यं येषां **A. Ca. C.**

**P. 333. l. 3. (173, 6.)** वृजनमिव । वृजनेः कर्त्तनार्थस्येदं रूपं **B.** वृजनमिव च मे वृजनेः कर्त्तनार्थस्येदं रूपं **A. C.**

**P. 333. l. 17. (173, 7.)** निमित्तेऽर्थे ॥ निमित्तेऽर्थं **A. B. C.**

**P. 333. l. 18. (173, 7.)** प्रयंतं ॥ प्रयंत इति **A. B. C.**

**P. 335. l. 21. (173, 11.)** तत्तस्वन ॥ तत्तसह **A. C.** तत्तसदनं **B.**

**P. 336. l. 10. (173, 12.)** योत्स्यामीति **B.** नोऽस्मभ्यमिति **A. C.**

## Critical Notes

**P. 338. l. 1. (174, 2.)** कातरत्वानिंदावन् ॥ कातरयदानिंदावन् B. कातरयत्वानिंदान A. C.

**P. 338. l. 2. (174, 2.)** तटकादीनि ॥ तयछकादीनि A. B. C.

**P. 338. l. 22. (174, 3.)** वस्तोर्वस्तुं ॥ वस्ता वस्तुं B. वस्तो: वस्तु A. C.

**P. 338. l. 24. (174, 3.)** यागाद्यनुष्ठानपर: स्यास्यामीत्यर्थ: ॥ यागाद्यनुष्ठानपुर स्यास्यामीत्यर्थ: B. यागाद्यनुष्ठानपरस्यास्यामीत्यर्थ: A. C.

**P. 340. l. 13. (174, 6.)** सचा सह श्रुती: क्षिप्रा हवि:प्रदानेन त्वयापत्यं B. त्वया सह श्रुती: क्षिप्रा हवि:प्रदानेन तथा अपत्यं A. C. The construction is wrong in both cases, unless we read वहमाना: संति instead of वहमाना ये संति ते प्रपश्यन्. Perhaps वहमाना: संति was the original reading, and ये प्रपश्यन् ते was added as a new sentence: or वाहमाना: । वाहमाना ये संति ते प्रपश्यन्.

**P. 340. l. 16. (174, 6.)** क्षिप्रा वर्जिता: ॥ क्षिप्रा वज्रिता: A. B. C.

**P. 341. l. 25. (174, 9.)** From here to 180, 7. (p. 360.) A. is wanting.

**P. 346. l. 21. (176, 2.)** ब्रीह्यादिकमुच्यते Ca. C. ब्रीह्यादिकमुच्यते B.

**P. 351. l. 12. (178, 1.)** श्रुतय: B. Ca. C. It ought to be श्रुती:, unless the whole sentence is taken as a parenthesis. Cf. Rv. vol. III. p. 191. l. 13.

**P. 352. l. 21. (178, 4.)** तथैव ॥ यथैव B. Ca. C.

**P. 355. l. 15. (179, 4.)** निमित्तात्कामात् । निमित्तांसत: कामात्कथं B. निमित्ता: संत: कामात्कथं Ca. C.

**P. 355. l. 26. (179, 5.)** The first part of this verse has been lost in the Commentary; none of the MSS. have preserved it. The words अस्मिन्पले etc. however, towards the end of the verse, seem to indicate that Sāyaṇa had given before an explanation of the words हत्सु पीतं. In the same verse (p. 356. l. 5.) B. has यद्वा यमपवजनीयतया, Ca. C. यद्वा यामपवजनीयतया. Again, instead of कामहत: सन् कामेन निरूद्ध एव, Ca. C. have कामहत: सन् नमिनानिरूद्ध एव, and B. कामहत: सन: कामिननिरूद्ध एव.

**P. 357. l. 9. (180, 1.)** दीयति तक्तीति ॥ दीयति टक्तीति Ca. C. दीयति तफ्फीति B.: cf. Nigh. II. 14.

**P. 357. l. 9. (180, 1.)** त्वदागमनकाले B. C.

**P. 358. l. 2. (180, 2.)** रथं प्रामुय इत्यर्थ: ॥ रथं प्राप्रथ इत्यर्थ: Ca. C. रथं वा श्रय इत्यर्थ: B.

**P. 359. l. 2. (180, 4.)** तन्नघर्मसकाशात् Ca. C. न पूर्वं धर्मसकाशात् B.

**P. 360. l. 1. (180, 5.)** सर्वप्रदेशव्यापित्वं ॥ सर्वप्रदेशवाचित्वं B. सर्वप्रदेशवाचत्वं Ca. C.

**P. 361. l. 18. (180, 8.)** After स इव all the MSS. have मध्ये. Either a whole sentence has been dropped, to which मध्ये belonged (संग्राममध्ये), or it was meant to follow after तेषु; तेषु मध्ये प्रशस्त: ॥

**P. 362. l. 1. (180, 9.)** वहत: A. B. C., instead of वहय:; a transition from the second to the third person, not unusual in Sāyaṇa.

**P. 362. l. 4. (180, 9.)** कर्मणि निवृत्ते पुनरपगच्छति ॥ कर्मण्यपवृत्ते पुनर्निगच्छति A. B. C.

**P. 365. l. 12. (181, 5.)** अन्यतमस्य A. B. C., instead of अन्यतरस्य, which would be more correct.

**P. 365. l. 23. (181, 6.)** वर्धिता एवेंद्र: ॥ वर्धिता देवेंद्र: A. C. वर्धिता देवेंद्र: B.

**P. 366. l. 21. (181, 8.)** स्तुतिवाक् Ca. C. B. स्तुतिर्वाक् A. Ca. sec. m. स्तुतिरूपा वाक् ?.

**P. 367. l. 1. (181, 8.)** शांतनात्सेके उदकस्येव ॥ शांतनात्सेके उदकस्यैव A. Ca. शांतनात्सेके उदके उदकस्येव

## Commentary (Sayana)

## Critical Notes

B. **शांतनात्सेके उदकस्येव** C. **शांतनात्** is probably a mistake; it may be meant for **शान्तवनात्** (‘because there is comfort, as if water was sprinkled’) or for **आप््यायनात्** (‘because there is growth’); but neither of the two emendations is probable.

P. 367. l. 8. (181, 9.) From here to 188, 6. A. is wanting. The Commentary from 184, 1. to 185, 5. however, is found in A 2. at the beginning of the seventh Adhyāya.

P. 368. l. 6. (182, 1.) **पालयितृधनौ** C. **पालायतृधनौ** B.

P. 370. l. 2. (182, 5.) **प्रसादफलकराश्विनौ** B. **प्रमादफलकराश्विनौ** Ca. **रोष्ट्रि** C.

P. 373. l. 2. (183, 3.) **यजमानाय दत्तहविषा तद्वान्** B. Ca. C. **यजमानदत्तहविषा तद्वान्** seems to be a necessary correction.

P. 381. l. 24. (185, 6.) **वृष्टादेः देवानां** Ca. C. **वृष्ट्या देवानां** B.

P. 382. l. 24. (185, 8.) **तयोरश्विन्यादिवहुमननासंभवाद्युचितमेव ॥ तयोरश्विन्यादिवहुमनासम्भवाद्युचितमेव** B. **तयोरश्विन्यादिवशमननासम्भवाद्युचितमेव** Ca. C. There is a mistake in this line, which the reading adopted in the text does not remove.

P. 386. l. 15. (186, 4.) **सर्वदैव वेत्यर्थः ॥ सर्वदैववार्थः** B. **सर्वदेववार्थः** Ca. C.

P. 389. l. 1. (186, 9.) **उत्पादयंति ॥ उत्पादयंतु** B. C.

P. 389. l. 2. (186, 9.) **सर्वेनामवृणोति** B. Ca. C. (**सर्वी द्यामावृणोति** or **सर्वमावृणोति**?) line 3. **मरुत्वेना हवृष्ट्या** B. Ca. C. **करोति** B. **करोतु** Ca. C.

P. 390. l. 4. (187, 1.) In Sāyaṇa’s quotation from Śaunaka’s Rig-vidhāna there are several readings differing from the MSS. of the Rig-vidhāna: **भुंजीत ह्यविकुत्सयन्** B. **भुंजीत ह्यवकुत्सयन्** Ca., but corrected into **भुंजीयादवकुत्सितं**, which probably would be found to be the reading of A. if a new A. MS. should be discovered. The MS. of the Rig-vidhāna, E. I. H. 1732 a. has **भुंजीयाद्विकुत्सितं**; 1732 b. has **भुंजीयादवकुत्सितं**. Again, **विषममप्यमृतं भवेत्** B. C.; but Ca. corrected (= A.) has **विषममप्यन्नतामियात्**, which is the reading of Rig-vidhāna 1732 b., while 1732 a. has **अमृतामियात्**. Instead of **नावाग्यतस्तु**, which is the reading of MSS. 1732 a. b., B. has **वक्तव्यमेव भुंजीत**, C. **वक्तव्याय च भुंजीत**, corrected into **न वक्तव्याय**.

P. 393. l. 15. (187, 9.) All the MSS. are so defective in this verse, that it is impossible to complete the sentence except by conjecture. B. reads **हे सोम ते तव यत् यमंशं गवां शिरः गोविकारः क्षीराद्याश्रयणद्रव्यं यवाशिरः यवविकाराश्रय शरीरं पीवो वभ ॥** Ca. has **हे सोम ते तव यत् यमंशं गवां शिरः गोविकारक्षीराद्याश्रयणद्रव्या यवाशिरः गोविकारक्षीराद्याश्रय शरीर पीवो भव ।** This has been corrected by marginal notes. First, after the last **श्र**, **णा** was put in, which, however, must have been meant to come in after **श्रय**; then this **णा** was blotted out, and a whole line put in after the same letter, **णाद्रव्या यव शिरः गोविकारक्षीराद्यश्रय**. The *á* of **द्रव्या** is again cancelled, and the whole emendation is erroneous, as it could only have been meant for **यवविकाराश्रयण**. But even after this there is no construction in the Commentary, and it is not clear even whether the Commentator referred **गवां शिरः** and **यवाशिरः** to **भजामहे** or to **ते**. To judge from the MSS., Sāyaṇa seems to have taken these words as accusatives dependant on

<meta>
This page is part of the Preface to Volume II of Max Müller's Rig-Veda-Sanhita. It discusses the "Khila" (supplementary or apocryphal) hymns of the Rig-Veda, citing evidence from Śaunaka's Anuvāka-anukramaṇī and other ancient texts to explain why they are excluded from the main numbering of the Shākala school. The page includes Sanskrit quotations in Devanagari and scholarly footnotes.
</meta>

## Preface Text

of what the Brahmans consider the canonical text of the Rig-veda. They are called ‘Khila,’ and in some MSS. ‘Parishishṭa.’ I have never met with them in the Pada-text of the Rig-veda, and some of the Sanhitá MSS. also omit them. Still some of them may claim a considerable antiquity; and though they are not included in the index of the hymns ascribed to Kátyáyana, there can be no doubt that they were known to Kátyáyana's predecessor, Śaunaka, who was the author of several Anukramaṇís to the Rig-veda. He mentions the Khilas in general in the introduction to his Anuváka-anukramaṇí:

-> एकैकमनुवाकं तु खिलानि ब्राह्मणानि च । संवत्सरे संवत्सरे पठेदरहरः शुचिः ॥ <-

Again, in the third verse of the same Anukramaṇí, between the 13th and 14th Anuváka of the first Maṇḍala, Śaunaka states distinctly that he does not enumerate the Khailika Anuvákas:

-> खैलिकानामनादेशोऽस्मिन् ग्रन्थेऽनुवाकानां । यस्तु चर्चायते वेदे तस्य संख्येति न श्रुतिः ॥<note>a</note> <-

Where the number of the Anuvákas, of the Súktas, the Vargas, the verses, the metres, and of the single words in the Rig-veda is given by Śaunaka (the words amount to 153826), the Khilas are never taken into account. But the very fact that they were not counted by Śaunaka, and that he himself says so, shows that they existed in his time. The number of hymns in the Śákala-śákhá is 1017, but, as Śaunaka says, exclusive of the Khilas: **सहस्रमेतत्सक्तानां निश्चितं खैलकैर्विना दश सप्त च पठ्यन्ते ।** The Bāshkala-śákhá, according to Śaunaka, contained eight hymns more, but again, as he says, exclusive of Khilas: **एतत्सद्दस्रं दश सप्त चैव ऋचावतो बाष्कलकेऽधिकानि । तान्यारण्ये शाकले शैशिरीये**<note>b</note> **वदंति शिष्टा न खिलेषु विप्राः ॥** Another proof of the antiquity of these Khila-hymns consists in their being quoted in the Nirukta<note>c</note>. In Páṇini the Khilas are not mentioned except in the Gaṇa-páṭha. Some of the verses which are Khilas in the Rig-veda occur in the text of the Átharvaṇa. In the Vájasaneyi-sanhitá several entire Adhyáyas are called Khila (XXVI—XXXV), and even in the latest works of the Vaidik period, in the Áraṇyakas and Upanishads, some portions are still marked as apocryphal. The 7th and 8th Adhyáya of the Bṛihadáraṇyaka are called Khila and Parishishṭa in the Commentary (p. 948. ed. Roer), and the whole Yájnikí Upanishad is called by the same name. In the epic poem of the Mahábhárata the Harivanśa is reckoned as a Khila.

As I did not insert the Khila-hymns in the printed text of the Rig-veda, I shall give them in the notes at the end of each Maṇḍala. They generally occur

## Commentary

The first of these verses, as my friend Dr. Aufrecht informs me, occurs in the Átharvaṇa X. 4, 9, though with considerable changes:

> अरसा इहाहयो ये अ॑ंति ये च दू॒रके । घ॒नेन॑ हन्मि वृ॒श्चिक॑म॒हं दं॒डेनाग॑तं ॥

The two last verses occur in the Mahábhárata I. 2190, with some slight alterations:

> सर्पसर्प भद्रं ते गच्छ सर्प महाविष । जनमेजयस्य यज्ञान्ते आस्तीकवचनं स्मर ॥
> आस्तीकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा यः सर्पों न निवर्तते । शतधा भिद्यते मूर्ध्नि शिंशपावृक्षफलं यथा ॥

-> **Maṇḍala II.** <-

At the beginning of the second Maṇḍala S 2. adds,

> विश्वेश्वर विरूपाक्ष विश्वरूप सदाशिव । शरणं भव भूतेश करुणां कर शांभव ॥

**P. 416. l. 4. (II. 1, 1.)** यद्वा आशु शीघ्रं शुच् दीप्तः सन् यतः स सेव्यत इति ॥ यद्वा आशु शीघ्रं शुचा दीप्तः सन् यतः संसेव्यत इति **A. C.** यद्वा आशु शीघ्रं शुच् दीप्तः सन् यतः स सेव्यत इति **B.** Perhaps आशु शीघ्रं शुचा दीप्त्या सन्यते सेव्यत इति.

P. 437. l. 20. (II. 4, 4.) Instead of **यद्वास्याग्नेः संबंधिनी पुष्टिर्यथा यजमानविषया रूपा तद्वत्**, Ca. C. have **यद्वास्याग्नेः संबंधिनी तद्वत् यद्वास्याग्नेः संबंधिनी पुष्टिर्यजमानविषया रूपास्तस्याग्नेः पुष्टिर्यया रूपा तद्वत् .**

P. 440. l. 22. (II. 5, 1.) **प्रयक्षन्.** The Pada has **प्रऽयक्षन्**, the Sanhitá **प्रयक्षं जेन्यं**; a final **न्** before palatals is written as Anusvára in most Vaidik MSS.

P. 441. l. 2. (II. 5, 1.) **यमं यमयितव्यं ॥ यमं यमेतव्यं** B. Ca. C.

P. 441. l. 3. (II. 5, 1.) **वाजिनोऽन्नस्य** B. Ca. C.

P. 444. l. 26. (II. 6, 2.) **स्तुत्युपनृहितेन ॥ स्तुत्यपबृहितेन** A. B. C.

P. 446. l. 26. (II. 7, 1.) **तेऽध्वर्य्यादिभिः ॥ ते ध्वर्य्यादिभिः** A. B. C.

P. 447. l. 9. (II. 7, 2.) **उभयविधाया द्विधः ॥ उभयविधायाः विद्धिषः** A. B. C.

P. 447. l. 9. (II. 7, 2.) **पूरय** A. C. **पूरयः** B. Although **परि** is explained in some passages by **पूरय** (cf. Rv. I. 174, 9), it was probably meant for **पालय** in our verse. See also Rv. I. 129, 5.

P. 447. l. 14. (II. 7, 3.) **धारा अल्पसुतीरिव त्मानात्नैवान्यनिरपेक्षेण ॥ धारा असस्तुरिव त्ना आत्मनैव अन्यनिरपेक्षेण** A. C. **धारा असस्तुरिव त्ना आत्मनैव अन्यनिरपेक्षेण** B. Sáyaṇa seems to have read **त्ना** instead of **त्वा**. **अल्पसुतीः** is merely conjectural, and not quite satisfactory because **सुतिः** is itself a Vaidik word. The whole may be a quotation, though this would hardly be in accordance with Sáyaṇa’s usual style of interpretation.

P. 447. l. 15. (II. 7, 3.) **अभिक्रम्य** A. B. C.

P. 447. l. 26. (II. 7, 5.) **सेकृभिः ॥ सेवभिः** A. C. deest in B.

P. 452. l. 23. (II. 9, 4.) **यद्वा मानयिता ॥ यद्वा मनोता** A. B. Ca. has **मनोता**, but the C. MSS. have **मानाता**, which, as it does not occur in Ca., is evidently a mistake of the first copyist; *o*, according to the old spelling, being frequently mistaken for *á* + *á*.

P. 455. l. 17. (II. 10, 4.) There is an omission in all the MSS. towards the end of the Commentary. After **घृतेन च** we expect the verb **जिहर्मि**, which I have inserted to complete the sentence, but instead of which the MSS. give extracts from a Bráhmana. In the usual style of Sáyaṇa such extracts would be preceded by **तथा च ब्राह्मणं**, while here all the MSS. begin at once and quite abruptly with the words **प्रति शेष**. Another irregularity is this, that the quotation from the Bráhmana refers not only to this, but also to the following verse. A. reads **घृतेन च प्रति शेष सर्वाणि भूतानि क्षेति पृथिव्या एष वयसा धूमेन वृहत्तं व्यचिष्ठमं रभसं दृशानमित्यनवकाशनवनमनन्नैरत्वांदी दीप्पमानमित्येतदा विश्वत इत्या सर्वतः प्रत्यचं जुहोतीत्येतदक्षरसेत्येहलमानेन मनसेदं जुषेतेत्येतन्मयश्रीरिति मर्यश्रीरित्येष स्मृहयद्वर्णो अग्निनो-**

<vocab>
मण्डल (Mandala), सूक्त (Sukta), अग्नि (Agni), सायण (Sayana), ब्राह्मण (Brahmana), अनुस्वार (Anusvara), पद (Pada), संहिता (Sanhita), रूपा (Rupa)

<meta>Page xxxvi of the Preface to Max Müller's Rig-Veda-Sanhita. This page details the critical process of restoring Sayana's commentary by comparing it with other Vedic texts. It features manuscript variants (Ca., B., C.) and lengthy citations from the Taittiríya-sanhitá (IV. 1), Taittiríyakam Bráhmaṇa (V. 1, 3, 2), and Vájasaneyi-sanhitá (XI) with Śatapatha-bráhmana commentary.</meta>

## Critical Notes

**भिमृश इति न ह्येष मृशेत दीप्यमानो भवतीति ॥** Ca. has **घृतेन च प्रति ह्येय सर्वाणि भूतानि क्षेति पृथिव्या एष वयसा धूमेन बृहन्तं** (sec. man. **तं**) **व्यचिटमन्वै रभसं दृशानमित्यनवकाशमवनमन्नै** (sec. man. **न्नै**) **रत्नार्दं** (sec. man. **र्दा**) **दीप्यमानमित्येतदा विश्वत इत्यादि सर्वतः प्रत्यंच** (**दीप्यमानं** struck out, but not in C.) **जुहोती** (**मी** C.) **त्येतदरक्षासेत्यहेलमानेन मनसेदं जुषेतत्यन्व्यश्रीरिति मयव्यश्रीरित्येष स्पृहयद्वर्णो अग्निनोभिमृश इति म** (sec. man. **न**) **ह्येष मृशेत दीप्यमानो भवतीति ।** The readings of the C. MSS. are the same as Ca. prima manu, with the exception of **दीप्यमानं**, which is left out in C., and **म** (sec. man. **न**), which is omitted. B. has **घृतेन च प्रति ह्येय सर्वाणि भूतानि क्षेति पृथिव्या एष वयसा धूमेन बृहन्तं व्याचिटमन्वै रभसं दृशानमित्यनवकाशवत्वमात्वरत्नार्दं दीप्यमानमित्येतदा विश्वत इत्या सर्वतः प्रत्यं** (sec. man. **त्यं**) **च जुहोमीयेतदरक्षासत्यहेलमानेन मसेदं जुषेतत्यन्व्यश्रीरिति मर्यव्यश्रीरित्येष स्पृहयद्वर्णो अग्निनोभिमृशेति न ह्येष मृशेत दीप्यमानो भवतीति ॥**

As it would have been difficult to restore the text from the MSS. of Sāyaṇa’s Commentary, it was necessary to collate the Bráhmaṇas, in which these verses are explained. Now the hymn in question is recited by the Hotṛi as part of the Prátaranuváka. We might therefore expect to find Bráhmaṇa explanations in the corresponding part of the Aitareya-bráhmana, II. 24—28. Here, however, no exegetical remarks are made on this particular hymn. As the Udgátri is not concerned with our hymn, we cannot expect to find an explanation of it in the Sáma-veda-bráhmana. The Adhvaryu priest has to use the first two verses of our hymn in the first part of the Agni-cayana sacrifice. These hymns, the Ukhásambharaṇa-mantras, are collected in the Taittiríya-sanhitá, IV. 1, and here accordingly we find our verse though slightly modified:

---

## Hymn Text (Taittiríya-sanhitá, IV. 1)

-> **जिघर्मि ॥ ४ ॥ अग्निं मनसा घृतेन प्रति ह्येष्यंतं भुवनानि विश्वा । पृथुं तिरश्चा वयसा बृहंतं व्यचिष्ठमन्नर रभसं विदानं । आ त्वा जिघर्मि वचसा घृतेनारक्षासा मनसा तज्जुषस्व । मर्यश्रीः स्पृहयद्वर्णो अग्निनोभिमृशे तनुवा जर्भुराणः ।** <-

---

## Commentary (Taittiríyakam Bráhmaṇa, V. 1, 3, 2)

The Bráhmaṇa to this is contained in the following, the fifth book of the Taittiríyakam (V. 1, 3, 2): 

> **जिघर्म्यग्निं मनसा घृतेनेत्याह । मनसा हि पुरुषो यज्ञमभिगच्छति ॥ प्रतिह्येष्यंतं भुवनानि विश्वेत्याह । सर्वह्येष प्रत्यङ् क्षेति ॥ पृथुं तिरश्चा वयसा बृहंतमित्याहल्पो ह्येष जातो महान् ॥ २ ॥ भवति ॥ व्यचिष्ठमन्नर रभसं विदानमित्याहान्नेनैवास्मै खदयति सर्वमस्मै खदते य एवं वेदा त्वा जिघर्मि वचसा घृतेनेत्याह । तस्मात्पुरुषो मनसाभिगच्छति तद्वाचा वदत्यरक्षसेत्याह रक्षसामपहत्यै ॥ मर्यश्रीः स्पृहयद्वर्णो अग्निरित्याहापचितिमेवास्मिन्दधात्यपचितिमान्भवति य एवं ॥ ३ ॥ वेद मनसा त्वेतामाहुतिमर्हति यामध्वर्युखग्नावाहुतिं जुहोति मनस्वतीभ्यां जुहोत्याहुत्यै द्वाभ्यां प्रतिष्ठित्त्यै etc.**

---

## Vedic Text & Commentary (Vájasaneyi-sanhitá & Śatapatha-bráhmana)

The last Veda which we can look for a Bráhmaṇa explanation is the White Yajur-veda. Here we find the two verses in question as 23 and 24 in the eleventh book of the Vájasaneyi-sanhitá, again with slight modifications. The corresponding Bráhmaṇa ought to be in the Ukhásambharaṇa of the Śatapatha-bráhmana, and here indeed we meet with explanations very similar to those given by Sāyaṇa. Prap. 3. Bráhm. 1. Kaṇḍiká 19. we read, 

> **आ त्वा जिघर्मि मनसा घृतेनेति । आ त्वा जुहोमि मनसा च घृतेन चेत्येतत् ॥ प्रतिह्येष्यंतं भुवनानि विश्वेति । प्रत्यङ् ह्येष सर्वाणि भुवनानि क्षियति ॥ पृथुं तिरश्चा वयसा बृहंतमिति पृथुवी एष तिर्र्यङ् वयसा बृहन् धूमेन व्यचिष्ठमन्नै रभसं दृशानमित्यवकाशवन्मन्नरत्नाह्र्दं दीप्यमानमित्येतत् ॥ १९ ॥ आ विश्वतः प्रत्यंच जिघर्मीत्या सर्वतः प्रत्यंच जुहोम्येतदरक्षसा मनसा तज्जुषेतत्यहेलमानेन मनसा तज्जोपयेतेत्येतन्मय्यश्रीः स्पृहयद्वर्णोऽग्निनोभिमृशे तन्वा जर्भुराण इति न ह्येपोऽभिमृशे तन्वा दीप्यमानो भवति ॥**

Although this is the Bráhmaṇa which Sāyaṇa must have had in his mind when
